style: Style: an original painting in the manner of a 19th-century Thai Buddhist temple mural (Rattanakosin era, like the ubosot walls of Wat Suthat and the Buddhaisawan Chapel): flat two-dimensional composition without Western perspective, fine gold-leaf contour lines, flat mineral pigments only (red ochre, indigo, malachite green, ochre yellow, chalk white, soot black), deep dark-green or dark red-brown background, stylised flame-shaped rocks and trees drawn leaf by leaf, slender graceful figures in classical Thai poses and gestures, pointed Thai crowns and ornaments, buildings with tiered Thai roofs, zigzag 'sinthao' lines separating the scene from the background. Painted on old temple wall plaster with faint fine cracks and slightly faded colour. Wide horizontal scene, main subject clearly readable in the centre, calm and reverent mood. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, not a cartoon, not a game. No text, no letters, no inscriptions, no signature, no border, no frame. Before the enlightenment Siddhartha is a human prince (fair skin, royal dress, pointed crown) or, after leaving home, a thin human ascetic in a plain saffron robe with short hair, no halo and no ushnisha. Only in scenes that explicitly name the Buddha, the enlightenment or the bodhi tree seat, show him in classical Thai mural iconography: golden body, small flame-shaped ushnisha on the head, simple serene face drawn in the traditional mural manner (not a portrait), saffron robe over the left shoulder, a soft halo; he is not the largest close-up element and is never comic.

items.renounce: Night. Prince Siddhartha, a young human prince with fair skin (not golden, no halo, no ushnisha), in white and gold royal dress and a tall pointed Thai crown, rides the white horse Kanthaka out through the tall gate of a walled Thai-style palace city; celestial beings (devata) hold the horse's hooves off the ground so they make no sound, his charioteer Channa holds the horse's tail and runs behind, stars and a crescent moon over dark blue sky, sleeping guards at the gate.
items.palace: The young prince seated in a pavilion of a splendid palace with three tiered-roof buildings for three seasons, court musicians and graceful dancers performing before him, lotus pond and gardens.
items.suddhodana: King Suddhodana, a dignified middle-aged Sakya king with a pointed crown, seated on a throne under a white tiered umbrella, courtiers kneeling before him.
items.procession: Queen Maha Maya, pregnant, travels in a golden palanquin carried by bearers, with a royal procession of attendants, parasols and banners along a road through countryside toward her home city.
items.birth: In the Lumbini grove of blossoming sal trees, Queen Maha Maya stands holding a flowering sal branch with her right hand, attended by kneeling ladies who hold up a cloth screen; celestial beings descend from the sky scattering flowers; a newborn baby glowing softly is received on a golden cloth by devas.
items.seven_steps: The newborn prince, glowing softly, takes seven steps toward the north, a large pink lotus blossoming under each footstep, celestial beings holding a white umbrella above him, devas in the sky scattering flowers, Lumbini sal grove behind.
items.ashoka_pillar: Emperor Ashoka with a royal retinue, elephants and parasols, erecting a tall polished sandstone pillar in the Lumbini grove, workers raising it with ropes, monks watching, sal trees around.
items.gotami: Queen Mahapajapati Gotami tenderly holding the infant prince in a palace chamber, attendants fanning, a lit oil lamp, calm and gentle.
items.asita: The old hermit Asita, with a long white beard, a tall coiled hair knot and a tiger-skin cloth, has come down from the mountains and holds the infant prince in his arms in the palace hall; he smiles with tears on his cheeks; King Suddhodana watches, Himalayan peaks drawn in the background.
items.naming: The naming ceremony: eight Brahmin sages in white robes seated before the king, who holds the infant prince; seven Brahmins raise two fingers, and the youngest Brahmin, Kondanna, raises only one finger.
items.jambu: At the royal ploughing festival, the young prince, about seven years old, sits alone in meditation under a large rose-apple (jambu) tree on a raised platform, the shade of the tree stays still over him; in the fields beyond, the king and nobles plough with decorated oxen.
items.wedding: The royal wedding of Prince Siddhartha and Princess Yasodhara seated side by side in a richly decorated pavilion, elders pouring blessing water, musicians and guests.
items.chariot: Prince Siddhartha rides out of the palace gate in an ornate horse-drawn chariot driven by the charioteer Channa, crowds of townspeople and stalls along the street.
items.sight_old: From his chariot the prince sees a very old man with white hair and a bent back, leaning on a walking stick by the roadside; Channa points toward him.
items.sight_sick: From his chariot the prince sees a sick man lying on a mat by the roadside, holding his stomach in pain, a relative kneeling beside him.
items.sight_dead: From his chariot the prince sees a funeral procession: a body completely wrapped in white cloth carried on a bamboo bier by mourners, relatives weeping; no visible wounds, dignified.
items.sight_monk: From his chariot the prince sees a calm wandering ascetic in a simple saffron robe with shaved head and an alms bowl, walking peacefully along the road; light falls on the ascetic.
items.sleeping_court: Night inside the palace hall: many female musicians and dancers asleep in disorder on the floor with their instruments scattered, oil lamps burning low; the prince stands up from his couch looking at them with a sober face.
items.farewell: Night. The prince stands at the open door of a bedchamber, looking in silently at Princess Yasodhara asleep on a bed with her arm around the newborn baby Rahula, a single oil lamp glowing; he does not enter.
items.mara_gate: Night at the city gate: Mara, a dark green-skinned demon king with a tall crown, floats in the sky and raises his hand to block the way, while the prince on the white horse Kanthaka rides on without turning back, Channa holding the horse's tail.
items.cut_hair: Dawn on the sandy bank of the Anoma river: the prince, kneeling, cuts his long topknot with his sword and throws it into the sky, where the god Indra receives it in a golden casket; Channa and the white horse Kanthaka wait nearby; his royal ornaments laid on the sand.
items.kanthaka: Channa walks back sadly leading the white horse Kanthaka, which looks back over its shoulder toward the distant figure of the ascetic in the forest; a river and dawn sky.
items.alms_rajagaha: The young ascetic Siddhartha in a simple saffron robe walks on alms round through the streets of Rajagaha, a city ringed by five hills, holding an alms bowl; townspeople stop and stare in wonder at his noble bearing; King Bimbisara's men watch from a palace balcony.
items.bimbisara: King Bimbisara of Magadha, with a pointed crown and retinue, kneels respectfully before the young ascetic seated on a rock at the foot of Pandava hill; servants present treasures and an elephant; the ascetic raises one hand gently in refusal.
items.teachers: The young ascetic Siddhartha in saffron robe sits respectfully before two elderly hermit teachers with white beards and coiled hair, seated in forest hermitages, other disciples meditating around them.
items.uruvela: A peaceful landscape at Uruvela: a clear river with sandbanks winding through a lush forest grove, a small village with grazing cattle, the young ascetic walking along the riverbank.
items.five_ascetics: Five ascetics in simple robes kneel and attend the young ascetic Siddhartha seated in the forest by a river; one of them, the eldest, Kondanna, offers water; birds and deer around.
items.austerity: The ascetic Siddhartha, extremely emaciated after years of fasting, seated in meditation in the forest, ribs and veins visible, eyes closed, still dignified and serene as in classical Thai murals of the austerities; animals nearby keep a respectful distance.
items.lute: The god Indra, green-skinned with a tall crown, floats in the sky playing a three-stringed lute (phin) beside the emaciated ascetic meditating in the forest below; one string is too tight and snaps, one too loose, one just right.
items.sujata: Morning under a large banyan tree: the young woman Sujata in fine dress kneels and offers milk-rice in a golden bowl to the ascetic Siddhartha seated under the tree; her maidservant kneels behind; cows nearby.
items.tray: The ascetic Siddhartha, standing at the edge of the river, places a golden tray on the water and it floats upstream against the current; ripples on the water, a naga king visible beneath the surface.
items.grass: Evening: the grass-cutter Sotthiya, a humble villager, offers eight bundles of kusa grass to the ascetic Siddhartha on the path near a great bodhi tree.
items.bodhi_seat: The Buddha-to-be seated cross-legged on a cushion of grass under a large bodhi tree with heart-shaped leaves, facing east, right hand reaching down to touch the earth (the earth-touching gesture), serene, golden aura. IMPORTANT gesture (bhumisparsha mudra, Thai: pang maravichai): his RIGHT hand hangs down over the RIGHT knee with the palm facing inward and the fingertips touching the ground in front of the seat; his LEFT hand rests palm-up in his lap. The right hand must clearly touch the earth.
items.mara_army: Mara's army attacks: Mara, a dark demon king with many arms and a tall crown, rides the giant war elephant Girimekhala, leading a vast host of demons with weapons, storm winds and rain through the sky toward the meditating figure under the bodhi tree, who remains calm in a golden aura.
items.thorani: Mae Thorani, the earth goddess, a graceful young woman in green with a crown, kneels below the Buddha, who is seated under the bodhi tree in the earth-touching posture (right hand resting on the right knee with fingertips touching the ground, left hand in the lap), and wrings her long hair, from which a great flood of water pours out and sweeps away Mara's army of demons and elephants on both sides; classic Thai mural Maravijaya scene. IMPORTANT gesture (bhumisparsha mudra, Thai: pang maravichai): his RIGHT hand hangs down over the RIGHT knee with the palm facing inward and the fingertips touching the ground in front of the seat; his LEFT hand rests palm-up in his lap. The right hand must clearly touch the earth.
items.enlightened: Dawn. The Buddha seated in meditation under the great bodhi tree, radiating rays of six colours in all directions, devas and celestial beings in the sky paying homage with flowers and music, the defeated Mara bowing in the distance.
